title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement: Bernardo chooses a three-digit positive integer \(N\) and writes both its base-\(5\) and base-\(6\) representations on a blackboard. Later LeRoy sees the two numbers Bernardo has written. Treating the two numbers as base-\(10\) integers, he adds them to obtain an integer \(S.\) For example, if \(N = 749,\) Bernardo writes the numbers \(10{,}444\) and \(3{,}245,\) and LeRoy obtains the sum \(S = 13{,}689.\) For how many choices of \(N\) are the two rightmost digits of \(S,\) in order, the same as those of \(2N?\)

solutions.text: Because \(\mathrm{lcm}(25, 36, 100) = 900,\) the condition on \(N\) depends only on \(N \bmod 900,\) so consider \(0 \le N \le 899.\) Let the last two base-\(5\) digits be \(a_1, a_0\) and the last two base-\(6\) digits be \(b_1,b_0.\) Modulo \(10,\) the desired equality and \(N\equiv a_0\pmod5\) force \(a_0=b_0.\) The Chinese Remainder Theorem applied modulo \(25\) and \(36\) then gives \[ \begin{aligned} N&\equiv180a_1+150b_1 \\ &\quad {}+a_0\pmod{900}. \end{aligned} \] Comparing twice this residue modulo \(100\) with the decimal number \(10(a_1+b_1)+a_0+b_0\) reduces to \(5a_1\equiv b_1\pmod{10}.\) Hence the valid pairs are exactly \((0,0),(2,0),(4,0),(1,5),(3,5).\) Each combines with \(5\) choices of \(a_0\) \((0 \le a_0 \le 4),\) giving \(25\) values of \(N.\) Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Since \(\mathrm{lcm}(5^2, 6^2, 10^2) = 900,\) the condition depends only on \(N \bmod 900,\) so let \(N\) range from \(0\) to \(899\)
Matching last digits forces the base-\(5\) and base-\(6\) units digits equal; working modulo \(100\) pins down the allowed last-two-digit pairs
